description.narrative: Projektet är ett svar på inrikesministeriets och det albanska polisväsendets förfrågan om att stödja en uppföljningfas av ”Community Policing in Albania”. Projektet kommer att genomföras av en konsult som kommer att väljas genom ett anbudsförfarande. Insatsen fokuserar på att förstärka säkerhets- och trygghetsinstitutionernas närvaro och roll i samhället, genom att öka deras ansvarsskyldighet och tillika förtroendet från medborgarna. Insatsen kommer att förbättra polisens hantering av brott i nära relationer, testa nya styrningsmetoder och delegera mer ansvar till två regionala poliskommissariat, förse det albanska polisväsendet med strategiskt styrningsstöd och skapa ett bidragsprogram för civilsamhällsorganisationer eller aktiva individer i Albanien med syfte att främja starkare band med polisen och förebygga våld i nära relationer. Insatsen som finansieras av Sverige kommer att genomföras under en fyraårsperiod, med en sammanlagd budget på 30 MSEK, med undantag för momskostnader för upphandling av utrustning som kommer täckas av Albanien. På den strategiska nivån, kommer insatsen att administreras av projektstyrkommittén som utgörs av de viktigaste intressenterna inom projektet.

The 2nd phase of the police cooperation in Albania seeks to help build mutual trust and partnership between police and communities with the ultimate goal to create safe neighbourhoods. In order to achieve this the programme will facilitate a number of behavioural changes necessary for a strong Community Policing approach. These include shifts in behaviour for individual officers , shifts in institutional behaviour within and across Community safety and security providers and shifts in behaviour within the communities. The contribution will be implemented over a four years period as a follow up of a first phase, and will be assigned to a consultant to be selected through an open tender. The implementation will be steered on strategic level from the Programme Steering Committee which will bring together the Ministry of Interior of Albania (MoI), the Albanian State Police (ASP), other relevant line ministries , civil society and Sida, through the Swedish Embassy.

The envisaged impact of the new programme is to build mutual trust and partnership between police and communities in order to create safe neighbourhoods. The direct outcomes for the programme envisage behavioural changes at a number of different levels, all of which are necessary to ensure a strong Community Policing approach. These include shifts in behaviour for individual officers , shifts in institutional behaviour within and across Community security and safety providers, and shifts in behaviours within the communities.

The program was organized in three interlinked pillars: Pillar 1 Support the ASP in enhancing the efficiency of the CP structure; strengthening local partnerships and capacity building for the staff. More concretely the objectives under this pillar were: A- Assist the Police especially at the TLPDs level to solve and prevent more crimes with the assistance and cooperation of CSS actors and the public. B- Contribute to an increased partnership and level of interaction across the different CSS actors and communities; work with all the elements of the Local Police Directorates (LPD) besides Community Policing (CP) designated police officers. C- Enhance the soft skills to interact with public and other institutions and strengthening or creating supporting systems. The bulk of support and efforts were directed towards pillar 1. As by design, the activities were mostly concentrated in TLPDs Elbasan and Kukës, piloted there and replicated to the other LPDs gradually. While two types of interventions, framework and capacity building, had a national scope, the improvement of working conditions was primarily concentrated in the two pilot LPDs of Elbasan and Kukës assigned as pilot/target regions. After evidencing the main discrepancies between EU countries models of Community Policing and that of Albania, the programme suggested improvements in the work division between Community Policing Officers (Zone inspectors) and other units like General Police Patrol, Control and Command Hall and Traffic Police, resulting in more focus of Community Policing officers towards prevention through risk assessment for their respective areas, trust and partnership building with the communities, communication, and releasing them from other non-specific tasks that were transferred to general Patrol and others. The new division, endorsed flexibly from ASP, was increased cooperation between different units and has resulted in a more effective performance of ASP as a whole. Under the new structure the Sector for Command and Control was strengthened, and a new Sector for Analysis and Monitoring was created in each LPD to support the director with information and analysis and to prepare strategic documents at the local level. A new position of CPO Educator and Work with the Youth was established in most commissariats to support preventive activities and run awareness raising campaigns especially with the schools. When implemented in practice the changes brought positive effect on the police officers and the way they perform their duties. However, to produce sustainable results, the changes should become part of the overall administrative routine and culture of the organization, and this remains a challenge. In urban areas it proved easier to adapt to the changes, while in rural areas the situation was more difficult, as these CPOs also carry out police patrol tasks. To make the changes effective the Programem has trained 985 police officers from different units on community policing and on the improvement of their day-to-day activities. Although traffic safety was part of the awareness raising campaigns in schools from the beginning, specific support was included in the program the last two years. This included awareness raising especially amongst the young in schools about traffic safety rules and behavior, material support through provision of speed radars and tablets for the police officers in the roads, and the development of a software that processes real-life fines for traffic violations by preventing the room for corruption and by enabling supervisors to monitor the work of patrols and traffic police and reorganize the deployment of officers to respond better to the needs and the situation in each area. Under pillar 1 a lot of focus was placed on prevention and awareness raising about 1. Drugs, Alcohol and Tobacco, 2. Traffic Safety and 3. Safety in school, including cybercrime and bullying. The programme has trained the Community Policing Officers who in turn CPOs managed to run almost 2.744 activities in a total of 269 schools and interacted with almost 85.000 pupils. Collaboration was created with the Ministry of Education and Science to deliver the programmes in schools. A special focus has been paid to the continuous improvement of the ASP service delivery to the citizens. Following the interventions from the first phase, to streamline business processes related to service delivery, creation of the Reception Halls concept and reconstruction of several premises in main commissariats, the project has continued the support in this area. All police services have been revised and further simplified, including the possibility to deliver them electronically. A new software for business processes management was elaborated and tested in Elbasan. It will allow for electronic management of most work processes, registration of different decision-making steps and the possibility to monitor the work performance of Reception Hall staff, but also the performance of staff involved in service delivery to the public. The Reports section of the software was developed to provide numerical and graphical presentation of the work completed. With shifting of all services online as of May 2022 this software becomes even more important for the workflow management in ASP. Pillar 2 Support strategic management in the ASP and implementation of the new Public Safety Strategy The specific objectives were: A- Assist the ASP to implement the Public Safety Strategy in parallel with management system that allows the organization to track their performance and be able to strategically deploy suitable resources in an effective and efficient manner. B- Enhance the internal coordination of the ASP. C- Improve the internal and external communication of ASP. The program has supported the preparation of strategic documents like the Community Policing Policy Paper and Action Plan 2018-2020 and reporting on the Public Order Strategy 2015-2020 which served as the basis for the elaboration of the new Public Safety Strategy 2021-2026, that guides the activities of the public order sector in these past years. The newly created Sector for Analysis and Monitoring in each LPD has extended the analytical and monitoring capacities at LPD level and enabled more effective decisions. All staff members have been trained by the programme. As a result, the staff has been enabled to elaborate reports and prepare informative notes on various topics for the managers. Unfortunately, the staff instability in these sectors has not allowed them to draw the maximum benefits from their work. A special attention has been paid to the continuous use of surveys and other information means related to the work of the police. The project has supported the organization of three rounds of the national Police Satisfaction Survey (2018, 2020 and 2022). The results of the 2018 round were largely discussed with various stakeholders and served as background material for the elaboration of the CP Policy Paper, while the results of the 2020 round were used to feed the Public Safety Strategy. The 2022 results were disseminated with all stakeholders and results will be used to plan activities for the coming years. Other surveys of smaller scale have been organized by the grant scheme projects. The most notable surveyed the opinion of Tirana citizens regarding the role of the police in the municipality compared to the other regions from May 2018 to September 2020. The program also implemented two rounds of the Local Safety Measurement System in Elbasan and Kukës regions and one additional round only in Elbasan. This tool is used to provide information related to public order in neighborhoods and guide the police and other stakeholders in taking the appropriate measures to address them. The results were discussed with the ASP and in meetings of the Local Councils of Public Safety in all municipalities in these two regions. The aim was to make all stakeholders aware of the public opinion and hold them accountable for their part of the job, which ultimately is about enhancing the partnerships and participation towards public safety. Strengthened partnerships and mutual trust between stakeholders and the police is one of the outcomes of the project. Therefore, the SCPA team embraced the Ministry of Interiors policy to establish the Local Councils of Public Safety (LCPS) in all municipalities. The focus of the program was in the pilot regions, although the support was spread to other municipalities through the grant scheme. The program contributed to the establishment of LCPS in 18 municipalities and supported some of these councils activities, by elaborating an annual plan of activities and training council members. Several meetings were initiated by the SCPA team and grantees to discuss different topics related to the communities. Although the MoI reports that these councils are created in most of the municipalities, the challenge remains to make these forums effective and to involve all stakeholders in ensuring safe neighborhoods. Feeding them with tangible results from their areas (using for example the LSMS surveys or other surveys) results in more structured meetings and focused discussions on the issues that concern the communities the most. Pillar 3 Domestic violence support and improvement of stakeholders skills; contribute to enhancing the interaction/ coordination among the ASP and other actors to ensure adequate and comprehensive treatment of domestic violence. The specific objectives under this pillar have been: A- Support the ASP to enhance the capacity to better respond to DV cases and also increase the coordination with other stakeholders dealing with domestic violence, with the focus on the range of preventative and responsive needs with regard to DV incidents. B- Contribute to enhancing the interaction/ coordination among the ASP and other actors to ensure necessary flexibility to ensure adequate and comprehensive (ample) treatment of domestic violence. activities have been organized in three fields: 1. Assessment and capacity development, 2. Creation and reinforcement of referral mechanisms for DV and 3. Awareness raising and improvement of working conditions. The program prepared recommendations for an ASP DV prevention approach, based on the assessment of the situation and in-depth interviews with stakeholders at HQ and in the three LPDs of Tirana, Elbasan and Kukës. The recommendations aim to improve the police response to this phenomenon, in the light of the latest amendment of the DV Law. A Capacity Development Plan related to DV needs was drafted in November 2019 and shared with the ASP specialists. It is designed to help a systematic development of the polices knowledge and skills required to respond to violence against women in an effective and appropriate manner. It consists of three essential pillars that correspond to critical tasks: establishing priorities of capacity-building needs, developing capacity building programs, and a management strategy that will allow these capacity-building programs to be implemented within the context of the budget and resource constraints. During November 2019 June 2022, in coordination with the ASP HQ, the SCPA program delivered 22 sessions of the training Legal Amendments in Addressing Domestic Violence for all the LPDs in the country with the participation of 508 CPOs and Crime Investigation Experts. The aim of the trainings was to provide state police officers with sufficient knowledge on the implementation of the latest changes and amendments regarding the preliminary immediate protection order and the conduct of risk assessment for domestic violence cases. The work on Community Coordinated Response to DV and the referral mechanisms was concentrated to 7 municipalities. This activity was carried out in close cooperation with ASP, Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and UN agencies (particularly UNDP and UN Women), using standardized procedure protocols.The Local Coordinators assigned in the municipalities as well as the Multidisciplinary Technical Team members have been trained and coached on the job.Through funds and projects of the Grants Scheme, local NGOs have been involved in this action by providing technical assistance and facilitate the process. Workshops and trainings have been organized in these municipalities, with the involvement of the representatives of Elbasan Referral Mechanism members (Elbasan is considered a good example of coordination and collaboration). The program has supported the ASP and MoI to carry out six awareness raising campaigns (2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2022) in the framework of UN Days of Activism Against Gender Based Violence. The target group of the campaigns has been the youth in many municipalities of Albania. The activities were attended by students of 95 high schools. 40 local NGOs, implementing Grant Scheme projects, were engaged in the process of coordination the campaign activities. With project funds the Interview Unit for Minors and Victims of Domestic Violence in Elbasan LPD underwent a complete reconstruction and refurnishing. In close coordination with the Swedish funded project on Juvenile Justice, technical requirements were prepared, and installation of state-of-the-art audio and video recording equipment was carried out. This was the first set of equipment of this type installed in Albania, enforcing the provisions of the Code for Criminal Justice for Children, allowing recording of the victims interview in the presence of defense lawyers and prosecutors. The entire interview can be recorded and be used as evidence at trial. A special software is installed to manage the information. In addition, an interview facility and a child-friendly interview room for minors and DV victims were completed in the reconstructed premises of Librazhd and Has Commissariats. In the framework of the Grants Scheme, two NGOs have supported the reconstruction and furnishing of the interview rooms for minors and DV victims in Commissariat 4 premises in Tirana and in the Administrative Unit No. 3 in Elbasan. The programme benefited from a horizontal component, the Grant Scheme, aimed to support the implementation of the activities in all three pillars and increase cooperation of all stakeholders at local level to improve safety in the communities. The objective of the Grant Scheme was to empower civil society organizations to embrace and implement the community policing philosophy and principles and support to combat DV. The GS projects aimed to enhance partnership and increase trust and confidence between the ASP and community, tackle the problems identified in the LSMS surveys and bring feedback to the LCPSs. Over the program lifespan N rounds of grants have been implemented and 73 winning projects awarded in main municipalities of Albania, spanning over 11 regions. Altogether, 1N3 project proposals were presented by NGOs from all Albanian regions, but Dibra. The overall contracted amount for the projects of all rounds is N04,472 Euro. The grant scheme proved once more to be an efficient method to bring the communities and the police closer, raise awareness on topics that concern the community and improve the overall safety in the communities. Partnerships have been formed, especially with the younger generation, which will yield effects in the years to come and will serve as a good prevention practice. Besides the envisaged activities, the intervention was able to conduct two other additional ones as a response to unforeseen situation in the country. The first relates to training and capacity building provided to the Programme partners on best application of methods and platforms of working online in the framework of COVID-19 restrictions. That enabled from police officers to civil society partners to continue their work and get the maximum out of the available instruments for remote working. It also gave a message of resilience and sustained commitment to all relevant parties. Also. as a response to the November 2019 earthquake, the SCPA project, following an approval from the Swedish Embassy, decided to support the reconstruction of a martyr police officers house damaged by the earthquake. The family was identified and selected in close cooperation with the Albanian State Police in Bushnesh village belonging to Thumana, as one of the worst hit areas and following the procurement procedures, the new house was delivered to the family.
